title: GATHER AS MUCH AS YOU NEED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Moses said to them, 'It is the bread the LORD has given you to eat. This is what
the LORD has commanded: "Everyone is to gather as much as they need. Take an
omer for each person you have in your tent."'" - Ex 16:15b-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"As much as they need." Not as much as they can carry, or as much as they can
get before their neighbour does.

That single phrase quietly dismantles a great deal of how we live. The measure is
need, not capacity and not comparison.

Notice the household element again: an omer for each person in your tent. The
strong gathered for the weak. A family with an elderly grandmother or a
newborn baby gathered on their behalf. Nobody was left to manage alone because
they could not gather for themselves.

There is a beautiful New Testament echo of this. Paul, urging the Corinthians to
give generously to poorer believers, quotes this very chapter: "The one who
gathered much did not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have
too little" (2 Cor 8:15). He applies the manna principle directly to Christian
generosity.

Notice too that they still had to go out and gather. God rained it down; they
bent down and picked it up. Provision does not remove effort; it makes effort
fruitful.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you measure what you need or what you could get?
2. Who in your circle cannot gather for themselves right now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, teach me to live by need rather than by appetite or comparison. Show me
whom I should be gathering for. Amen.
